title: Cartesian associative algebras and Segal simplicial objects
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cocartesian fibrations and edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], the simplex category and inert maps of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], and the cartesian monoidal envelope of [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope]. Let $\mathcal C$ be an infinity category with finite products, including a terminal object for the empty product. Write $\mathsf{Fin}_*$ for finite pointed sets and $\langle n\rangle=\{*,1,\ldots,n\}$. Choose the product-diagram model $\mathcal C^\times\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ and its coherent product-evaluation functor $\pi:\mathcal C^\times\to\mathcal C$ from [lem-coef-cartesian-envelope-product-diagram-recognition]: a tuple has image its product, and an arrow has image the tuple of its block maps precomposed with the input projections.

Let $\mathsf{Ass}$ be the ordinary symmetric operad with one color whose operations on a finite labeled input set are its linear orders; substitution concatenates the ordered input lists, the nullary operation is the empty list and the unary identity is the singleton list. Its category of operators $\mathsf{Ass}^\otimes$ has objects $\langle n\rangle$, and a morphism is a pointed map together with a linear order on each non-basepoint fiber; composition substitutes these lists and discards inputs sent to the basepoint. Write $u:\mathsf{Ass}^\otimes\to\mathsf{Fin}_*$ for the forgetful functor. Put $\mathcal C^\times_{\mathsf{Ass}}=\mathcal C^\times\times_{N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)}N(\mathsf{Ass}^\otimes)$. Let $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathsf{Ass}}(\mathcal C^\times)$ denote the full infinity category of sections of this pullback carrying inert arrows to cocartesian arrows, with coherent transformations over the identity of the base; inert means that each non-basepoint output has exactly one preimage.

Define $\operatorname{Cut}:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{Ass}^\otimes$ by $\operatorname{Cut}([n])=\langle n\rangle$. For $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$ with opposite $a:[m]\to[n]$, it sends $j$ to $i$ if $a(i-1)<j\leq a(i)$ and to $*$ otherwise, ordering each fiber by its input indices. Let $\mathcal C^\times_{\mathrm{pl}}$ be the pullback along $N(\operatorname{Cut})$, and let $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathrm{pl}}$ be its infinity category of inert-preserving sections, in the nonsymmetric convention of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category]. Let $\operatorname{Mon}_\Delta(\mathcal C)$ be the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}),\mathcal C)$ on diagrams $F$ whose inert edge maps exhibit $F([n])\simeq F([1])^n$ as a product cone for every $n\geq0$.

Restriction along $N(\operatorname{Cut})$ induces an equivalence $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathsf{Ass}}(\mathcal C^\times)\simeq\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathrm{pl}}$. Composition with the specified $\pi$ after restriction induces an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathsf{Ass}}(\mathcal C^\times)\simeq\operatorname{Mon}_\Delta(\mathcal C).$$
These equivalences preserve the underlying-object functor to $\mathcal C$. They identify the $r$-ary operation $x^r\to x$ for the standard input order with the transport along the endpoint-preserving arrow $[r]\to[1]$, under the Segal product cone; arity zero gives the unit. They identify the entire infinity categories, including mapping spaces and all higher families. For an algebra morphism with underlying map $f:x\to y$, the corresponding transformation has degree-$n$ component $f^n$ under the product-cone identifications. The equivalences are natural in finite-product-preserving functors. No other limits or any colimits are required.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Construction 2.1.1.7 and Definition 4.1.1.3 / Remark 4.1.1.4 (the ordered-fiber associative operator category), Proposition 2.4.2.5 (composition with the cartesian-structure functor), Construction 4.1.2.9 (Cut), Proposition 4.1.2.10 (restriction of associative monoids), and Definition 4.1.3.16 and Proposition 4.1.3.19 (planar algebra restriction). Read in the retained sandbox HA.txt. Source archive WANTED in report.md; no Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical comparison. The statement contains only these standard comparison equivalences; tree/forest reconstruction is supplied by the existing colored-operation-section node in the item proof.

proof.text: Identify the pure-algebra ordinary category underlying $A$ in [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding] with $\mathsf{Ass}^{\otimes}$ by sending $(\langle n\rangle,\varnothing)$ to $\langle n\rangle$. For these objects the module-input restrictions are vacuous, so both Hom sets consist of exactly the same pointed maps and ordered non-basepoint fibers. Both compositions concatenate the same lists, and both inert classes are the singleton-fiber maps. This is an isomorphism over $\mathsf{Fin}_*$, not an identification of the image of Cut with $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. The formulas for Cut on objects and ordered blocks agree under it.

source.place: Construction 2.1.1.7; Definition 4.1.1.3 and Remark 4.1.1.4; compare the pure-algebra part of Construction 4.2.1.1

proof.text: By the Cut clause of [lem-coef-lm-prism-approximation], the resulting $N(\operatorname{Cut}):N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})\to N(\mathsf{Ass}^{\otimes})$ is an approximation and induces an equivalence on the color fiber. The same node identifies its marked edges exactly with opposites of interval inclusions. Indeed, for $a:[m]\to[n]$ the fiber over output $i$ is $(a(i-1),a(i)]$; it is a singleton for every output precisely when $a(i)=a(0)+i$. For $m=0$ this condition is vacuous and every vertex inclusion is an interval inclusion. Thus the marking is exactly the nonsymmetric inert class in [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category]. The approximation is used in its categorical-fibration-replacement sense; Cut itself need not lift permutations and is not asserted to be a categorical fibration.

Check the target of approximation restriction. Write $P=\mathcal C^\times$ in the specified product-diagram model. [lem-coef-cartesian-envelope-product-diagram-recognition] gives its cocartesian fibration, fibers $\mathcal C^n$, output mapping-space products, and its exact blockwise cocartesian criterion. Pull back first to $N(\mathsf{Ass}^{\otimes})$ and then to $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$; [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] gives these base changes as cocartesian fibrations, represented by the stated simplicial pullbacks. They have the same fibers and block formulas. Over an ordered operator the mapping space is the product of its output block mapping spaces; for an inert operator each block has one input. Consequently the pullback to Ass has the fiber and output Segal properties required of the operadic fibration in [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction]. It is categorical: for a permutation in the base, permute the tuple and its subset product diagram; the resulting edge and its inverse have identity singleton block maps, and their compositions are the identity diagram. Hence every base equivalence lifts to an equivalence. Inner lifting is part of the cocartesian-fibration condition. On the planar pullback an inert edge is cocartesian precisely when these same singleton block maps are equivalences, so the two required markings agree. This verifies the target hypotheses, including arity zero, before applying the restriction theorem.

source.place: Remark 4.1.3.11; Definition 2.1.2.13; use the explicit cartesian product-diagram model in the statement

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction] to the approximation of step 2 and the operadic fibration of step 3. Its section category is exactly $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathsf{Ass}}(\mathcal C^\times)$, and its category of marked lifts is exactly $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathrm{pl}}$: a lift to the Ass pullback is the same simplicial map as a section of the planar pullback, and step 2 identifies the inert markings. The resulting equivalence is the specified precomposition by Cut, including coherent transformations over the identity base and their higher simplices. It has not been deduced merely from a bijection on algebra operations.

Apply [lem-coef-generalized-cartesian-product-cones] with $\mathcal M=N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ and its identity projection. The source hypotheses hold directly: every fiber is a point, every inert arrow is a cocartesian lift for the identity, and every mapping space over a prescribed base arrow is a point. Thus the edge and vertex incidence diagrams consist of points and satisfy their limit axiom; the zero fiber is the one-point Kan complex. The algebra category in that lemma is therefore $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathrm{pl}}$. Its product-cone subcategory is precisely $\operatorname{Mon}_\Delta(\mathcal C)$, since the color restrictions at $[n]$ are the $n$ maps $\rho_i:[n]\to[1]$, and the empty product condition is terminality at $[0]$. Use the product-diagram realization of the cartesian envelope: the total-product functor of the lemma is represented here by full-subset evaluation $\pi$, as specified in [lem-coef-cartesian-envelope-product-diagram-recognition]. On a simplex its product cone and block comparisons are the restrictions of that model's relative-exponential evaluation. To account for choices of products, apply [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] to the diagonal $\mathcal C\to\mathcal C^I$ for each finite output set $I$: the product mapping-space property is exactly its universal-arrow hypothesis. Its arbitrary-parameter clause makes the projection-preserving comparison of product choices coherent on every base simplex, compatibly on faces and degeneracies; its contractible-choice clause identifies the two realizations. Thus composition with the specified $\pi$ is the product-cone equivalence of the cited theorem. Composing it with step 4 gives the required second equivalence; no additional limits or colimits have been introduced.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.2.5; the planar instance of the cartesian product-cone argument preceding Proposition 4.1.2.10

proof.text: Let $x$ be the color value of a section. The singleton projections identify its value at $\langle n\rangle$ with the tuple $(x,\ldots,x)$; evaluation by $\pi$ gives $x^n$, including the terminal object for $n=0$. Since Cut sends $[1]$ to the color and $\pi$ on the one-factor fiber is its given evaluation equivalence, both comparisons commute with the underlying-object functor. The endpoint-preserving $[r]\to[1]$ has one ordered block containing every input, so its component is the standard-order operation $x^r\to x$ by the block formula of [lem-coef-cartesian-envelope-product-diagram-recognition]. For $r=0$ its sole block is empty and gives the unit. For a transformation with color component $f:x\to y$, naturality at every $\rho_i$ gives $\operatorname{pr}_i\eta_n\simeq f\operatorname{pr}_i$. The product-cone universal property identifies this entire coherent tuple of components with $f^n$; the parametric clause of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows], with $I=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, includes the comparison homotopies and all higher parameter simplices. For $n=0$ both sides are the unique map of terminal product cones.

source.place: Definition 4.1.2.5 and Remark 4.1.2.6; explicit evaluation of Construction 4.1.2.9

proof.text: The comparison on all transformations and higher families is already part of [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction] and [lem-coef-generalized-cartesian-product-cones], so their composite is an equivalence of the full stated infinity categories, with their mapping spaces. Naturality in a finite-product-preserving $h:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ follows from the coordinatewise strong functor $h^\times$ of [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope], the target naturality of approximation restriction, and the coefficient-functor naturality of the product-cone equivalence. The comparison $h\pi_{\mathcal C}\simeq\pi_{\mathcal D}h^\times$ is the product comparison on every tuple; it preserves the specified projection cones. [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] supplies its compatible arbitrary-parameter product comparisons, so it commutes coherently with all block maps, including empty blocks, and not only with their values on objects. These are exactly the naturality comparisons of the two equivalences. All indexing nerves are small after the universe enlargement allowed in the statement, and the only limits used in $\mathcal C$ are finite products.

source.place: Propositions 2.4.2.5 and 4.1.3.19, naturality of their specified composition and restriction functors
